newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen sees better profit, stable payout.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen sees better profit, stable payout.

text.p: German steel group Thyssen AG said on Tuesday profits would rise in the 1996/97 business year and it hoped to pay an at least unchanged dividend after cutting its payout to eight marks last year.
Thyssen, which announced a jump in pre-tax profits in the six months to March 31 to 631 million marks from 349 million marks, said it expected its business to pick up in the second half.

The company also said restructuring measures were already starting to bear fruit and lead to an improved result this year in its trading and services and capital goods divisions to a noticeable rise in earnings.
Thyssen said its steel business would also post a clearly positive result, although it was not yet clear whether the division would match its year-earlier result.

The company last year announced a strategy to spin off non-core businesses and focus on its five main business areas. It has also agreed to merge its steel operations with Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.
